chapters.title: Prologue
chapters.html:
2nd Book of the Covenant 1

The Testament of Our Lord and Savior Jesus Christ

1As for me, I have seen, from the outside to the inside, the appearance and the reality, twice unheard of and marvelous: justice given to each according to his works.

Notes

  • The whole book — worked from the French of L. Guerrier with S. Grébaut, Le Testament en Galilée de Notre-Seigneur Jésus-Christ (Patrologia Orientalis 9, 1913), which is translated from the Ethiopic. No Ge'ez or other source language was used. The chapters are Guerrier's numbered sections; each verse is one of his paragraphs. From section 12 on, M. R. James's English of the same text (1924) is read beside the French; James follows the Coptic where it survives, so where the two differ the French, which is the Ethiopic, is followed.

  • The heading — the manuscript's own title. Guerrier renders its first word Testament; the book's place in the canon gives the same word as Covenant, and the Ethiopian canon counts this book as the second Book of the Covenant.

  • v1 "As for me, I have seen" — the speaker is not named, and the sentence does not say who is speaking or what was seen beyond the appearance and the reality. Guerrier notes on the page that this prologue has only a very obscure sense and does not join naturally with what follows. The rendering stays as close to his French as English allows: du dehors au dedans, l'apparence et la réalité doublement inouïes et merveilleuses.

  • Source text — L. Guerrier and S. Grébaut, Le Testament en Galilée de Notre-Seigneur Jésus-Christ, Patrologia Orientalis 9.3 (1913), public domain. English translation by this project.

speech.text: 2nd Book of the Covenant 1
The Testament of Our Lord and Savior Jesus Christ
As for me, I have seen, from the outside to the inside, the appearance and the reality, twice unheard of and marvelous: justice given to each according to his works.

chapters.title: The Fate of Sinners
chapters.html:
2nd Book of the Covenant 2

Predictions of the End of the World

1The account our Lord Jesus gave His eleven disciples in Galilee, after He had risen from the dead, saying: "Listen, sons of light, pay attention to the word of your Father. I will reveal to you what will happen in the world, so that those who believe in Me may fear when they learn it. As for the sinners who will not believe in Me, they will not know My own signs, but My friends will know them. The sinners will be driven to the flame of torment and handed over to the fire that will punish their understanding. For Gehenna has opened its mouth and wished its belly to be full. Its roots will be torn out, its fruits gathered: they are the destruction of the sons of men, for their ungodliness has led them to destruction. Their fault is hidden in the days of their life, but on the last day it will be uncovered, for their ungodly word will be heard and will itself rebuke them. The world will be heavy for them because their days are few, and I Myself will not give them help.

Notes

  • v1 "Gehenna has opened its mouth" — Isaiah's picture of the grave: Sheol has opened wide its throat, and opened its mouth beyond measure (Isaiah 5:14).

  • Source text — L. Guerrier and S. Grébaut, Le Testament en Galilée de Notre-Seigneur Jésus-Christ, Patrologia Orientalis 9.3 (1913), public domain. English translation by this project.

chapters.html:
2nd Book of the Covenant 3

1"The kingdom of the East will be destroyed and clothed in mourning, and the West will prepare itself for ruin; the South will be terrified, and the North will listen and fall apart. The other lands that remain will be destroyed when the Judgment draws near, when the Scriptures are fulfilled and the days draw near.

chapters.title: Signs in Heaven and on Earth
chapters.html:
2nd Book of the Covenant 4

1Our Lord said to us, "Signs and wonders will happen in heaven and on earth before the end of the world comes."

2We said to our Lord, "Explain them to us and show them to us."

3He said to us, "To you I will indeed explain and teach these signs. It is not you who will see what is to happen, but those you yourselves have taught, those who will believe in Me. Then My faithful, and those who will not believe as well, will hear the blast of a trumpet coming from heaven to the earth, and they will see stars falling like fire, and great stars appearing in the daytime. A star that appears from the East will look like fire. The sun and the moon will be at war: always the terror and dread of thunder, of lightning and of the crash of thunder, always earthquakes. Cities will fall, and people will die under their ruins. There will be earthquakes continually, because the water has gone: the deeps will be dried up, the rivers will vanish, and the sea will draw back. A great plague will come, and death for many, until there are not enough funerals for those who die, and war comes of children with their parents in the same —. Kin will despise kin, and no one will turn to another. Those who have been abandoned will rise; they will see those who abandoned them, and will not pull them out of their trouble; for ruin itself, suffering and envy, once they have taken hold of a man, will bring him to hatred. People will lament over those who did not listen to the Lord's commandment. Then My heavenly Father will be angry because of the wickedness of men; for through the corruption of their impurity, the faults they have plotted have been many, so that the prophecy may be fulfilled that says: I have seen you when you ran with the thief, when you sat with the fornicator, when you insulted your mother's child, when your tongue wove wickedness and you caused great offense to your mother's child. What did you suppose? That I would become like you, that I would be the witness of your work?

4This is what I tell you. You, for your part, tell Israel and the nations to listen and believe, so that they may be saved and flee far from the wrath and the flame of fire that are coming. Hear this too, sons of light: as soon as the Lord comes, when He draws near, the angels will withdraw from the fruits, the rivers, the deeps and the trees, and a burning heat will come on the fruits. What remains after the heat, the large locusts and the small locusts will eat; what the small locusts leave, the middle locusts will eat.

5Then, moreover, when the Perverse One has drawn near, Satan will speak and sing to the four corners of the world.

Notes

  • v3 "the prophecy that says: I have seen you when you ran with the thief" — the psalm of God's judgment: When you see a thief, you are pleased with him, and your portion is with adulterers… you slander your own mother's son… you thought I was altogether like you (Psalm 50:18–21).

  • v4 "the large locusts and the small locusts… the middle locusts" — Guerrier names the three by size, and notes that the Ethiopic words answer to the Greek akris and brouchos and to the Hebrew locust names of Joel: What the cutting locust left, the locust has eaten; what the locust left, the young locust has eaten (Joel 1:4).

  • Source text — L. Guerrier and S. Grébaut, Le Testament en Galilée de Notre-Seigneur Jésus-Christ, Patrologia Orientalis 9.3 (1913), public domain. English translation by this project.

chapters.title: Against the Nations of Asia Minor
chapters.html:
2nd Book of the Covenant 5

1"Then Syria will be taken captive and will lament over her sons. Cilicia will lift up her neck, until the one who will judge her appears. Rise, you who sit on a throne, you who rest in glory, daughter of Babylon: drink what has been drawn for you. Then, Cappadocia, Phrygia, Lycaonia, bow your backs in your own land, for many peoples will trample you underfoot. Then the camps will open and the armies will go out, and they will surround the whole earth; then they will destroy the temples of Armenia. Pontus and Bithynia, your young men will fall by the edge of the sword, your sons and your daughters will be captives, and the walls of Pontus will weep. The rivers of Lycaonia will be mixed with blood. You, proud Pisidia, who trust in riches, you will vanish into the earth and be trampled underfoot because of your works. That is why I will raise up kings against you for destruction, and they will shed your blood; and your soul will be with the souls of those who go down into Gehenna. Pamphylia and all the coast, gird your loins with bronze and iron, and hide the strangers; prepare ships for flight: the sea will become a tomb for those who remain in you. As for Phoenicia, the sword will enter her, because she has borne sons of destruction. Judea, clothe yourself in groaning, raise your walls, open your gates, widen your enclosure, adorn yourself with the ornaments of youth, make yourself beautiful for your beloved, prepare your throne for your king, prepare yourself for the day of corruption: your affliction will come.

Notes

  • v1 "Rise, you who sit on a throne… daughter of Babylon" — Isaiah's word to the same city turned the other way: Come down and sit in the dust, virgin daughter of Babylon; sit on the ground without a throne (Isaiah 47:1). Here she is bidden to rise from her throne and drink.

  • Source text — L. Guerrier and S. Grébaut, Le Testament en Galilée de Notre-Seigneur Jésus-Christ, Patrologia Orientalis 9.3 (1913), public domain. English translation by this project.

chapters.title: The Antichrist
chapters.html:
2nd Book of the Covenant 6

1Then He spoke about the Deceiver. He told us that this Deceiver is the Antichrist, who will count us among the —; for his coming is for destruction. The hour is near; he is coming, and the road is opening for him. A glowing sword is in his hand; his anger and his indignation are fire, the weapon of torment. He is the one who arranges evil, who was born for corruption, who — blood; for his strength is deception, his hand is given to trickery, his right hand is torture and his left hand darkness. This is what marks him: his head is like a flame of fire, his right eye is shot with blood, his left eye is dead, the two pupils of his eyes are white in their lids, his lower lip is large, his feet broad, his fingers and the joints of his feet twisted. He is the scythe of destruction: the time has come, the harvest is near; he will reap those he must, for torment, and to many he will present himself as the Christ. He will praise himself and his works, and confirm the thinking of his mind.

Notes

  • v1 "who will count us among the — … who — blood" — the text held here is damaged in two places: a word is lost after count us among the, and the verb before blood. The gaps are left open.

  • Source text — L. Guerrier and S. Grébaut, Le Testament en Galilée de Notre-Seigneur Jésus-Christ, Patrologia Orientalis 9.3 (1913), public domain. English translation by this project.

chapters.title: The Sign for the Chosen
chapters.html:
2nd Book of the Covenant 7

1"Then the Lord will appear to those who have trusted in Him. When He comes, a great sign will appear, so that only My friends will know it, those who have kept the commandments of My Father and have rejected gold and silver, the riches of this world and the goods of this earth. Those I Myself will receive on that day. Their faces will shine seven times brighter than the light of the sun. I Myself will be their God, and they will be My people; I Myself will be their Father, and they will be My sons and daughters. I will be the altar for them, and they will be the temple for Me. I will make known to them the will of My Father and the judgment of this world; I will place them with My angels, and they will rejoice for thousands of years, more than their own selves; for they suffered in the middle of the world that deceives, and hated every state of rest.

Notes

  • v1 "I Myself will be their God, and they will be My people… My sons and daughters" — the promise Paul strings together for the Corinthians: I will be their God, and they will be My people… I will be a father to you, and you will be My sons and daughters (2 Corinthians 6:16, 18). Here the Son says it, and adds I will be the altar for them, and they will be the temple for Me.

  • Source text — L. Guerrier and S. Grébaut, Le Testament en Galilée de Notre-Seigneur Jésus-Christ, Patrologia Orientalis 9.3 (1913), public domain. English translation by this project.

chapters.title: The Wicked
chapters.html:
2nd Book of the Covenant 8

1"Many are those who reject and abandon the commandments of the Lord and persecute the righteous, the righteous who are tormented by those who love this world. They will be handed over to the torment of burning flames of fire, which will consume the desires of their hearts. Many too are those who will take My will to demand sacrifices and slaughterings of animals, and will shed blood in My own name, as though offering it as an oblation for their sins; acting so, they will treat Me as an idol. Yet through the prophets I commanded their fathers not to eat the flesh of a carcass, and not to drink the blood of a carcass. For they, because they are fleshly, Me —

Notes

  • v1 "they, because they are fleshly, Me —" — the text held here breaks off at the foot of a page, and the next chapter begins a new section. The break is kept.

  • Source text — L. Guerrier and S. Grébaut, Le Testament en Galilée de Notre-Seigneur Jésus-Christ, Patrologia Orientalis 9.3 (1913), public domain. English translation by this project.

chapters.title: Against the Bishops and the Priests
chapters.html:
2nd Book of the Covenant 9

1"But My judgment will come on the bishops and the priests, for they have led My people astray for the sake of their own pleasure. Through the prophet Isaiah too I had set it out for them and said: I have ordered weeping, lamentation, and girding with sackcloth; but they have made merry, slaughtering oxen and sacrificing sheep, and saying, 'Let us eat and drink, for tomorrow we die.' This has been made known in the ears of the Lord Almighty. Their sin will not be forgiven them until they die. For the sacrifice of the Lord is a gentle spirit, a gentle and pure heart; this sacrifice the Lord does not despise. Turn, then, to Me, all of you, and I too will turn to you, says the Lord Almighty.

2Do not become like your fathers, of whom the prophets speak, who ate the manna in the wilderness and did not know the grace of the Lord. It was not known to them, for they longed for meat and were filled according to the evil desire of their hearts. As the Lord has said: My people have eaten meat and drunk wine; they have grown fat and gross; they have kicked My beloved; the priest and the prophet themselves have raved because of wine. But the sons of Jonadab son of Rechab never drank wine, and kept the commandments of their fathers.

Notes

  • v1 "Let us eat and drink, for tomorrow we die… will not be forgiven them until they die" — Isaiah 22:12–14: the Lord GOD of hosts called for weeping and mourning… but instead there was joy and gladness, killing oxen and slaughtering sheep… "Let us eat and drink, for tomorrow we die." … "Surely this iniquity will not be atoned for you until you die." The words on the sacrifice the Lord does not despise are Psalm 51:17, The sacrifices of God are a broken spirit, where the Ethiopic as Guerrier gives it has gentle.

  • v2 "the sons of Jonadab son of Rechab never drank wine" — the Rechabites of Jeremiah: We will drink no wine, for Jonadab son of Rechab our father commanded us (Jeremiah 35:6), held up there, as here, against a people that did not keep its Lord's word.

  • Source text — L. Guerrier and S. Grébaut, Le Testament en Galilée de Notre-Seigneur Jésus-Christ, Patrologia Orientalis 9.3 (1913), public domain. English translation by this project.

chapters.title: Exhortation to the Apostles
chapters.html:
2nd Book of the Covenant 10

1"That is why I tell you: remain in the fear of the Lord and in righteousness, for you brought nothing into this world, and you must go out of this world naked. So gain righteousness alone, and the love of the Lord.

Notes

  • v1 "you brought nothing into this world" — Paul's words to Timothy, for we brought nothing into the world, and we cannot take anything out of it (1 Timothy 6:7).

  • Source text — L. Guerrier and S. Grébaut, Le Testament en Galilée de Notre-Seigneur Jésus-Christ, Patrologia Orientalis 9.3 (1913), public domain. English translation by this project.

chapters.title: The Righteous Persecuted
chapters.html:
2nd Book of the Covenant 11

1"For when the world is at its end and the last days draw near, the wicked will rise up; they will persecute those who fear the Lord, and the righteous. They will punish them as they please, for their understanding will be blind. The sinners will quarrel with the righteous, persecute them, hate them, and speak every evil word against them. That is why the Lord will throw them into the fire that is not put out and to the worm that does not sleep. Then every creature will come to the burning of the fire, for the sun and the moon will no longer give their light, the waters will fail, the rivers will dry up, the heaven will be rolled up, and the earth will be struck. The Lord will rise to judge His people, to repay each of them according to his works and according to the words they have spoken, on the way of righteousness. The righteous, who have walked in the way of righteousness, will inherit the glory of the Lord and His power; they will be given what the eye has not seen and the ear has not heard, and they will rejoice in My kingdom."

Notes

  • v1 "the worm that does not sleep… what the eye has not seen and the ear has not heard" — the end of both roads in the Lord's words and Paul's: where their worm does not die, and the fire is not quenched (Mark 9:48); What no eye has seen and no ear has heard… what God has prepared for those who love Him (1 Corinthians 2:9). With this the prophecy spoken in Galilee ends.

  • Source text — L. Guerrier and S. Grébaut, Le Testament en Galilée de Notre-Seigneur Jésus-Christ, Patrologia Orientalis 9.3 (1913), public domain. English translation by this project.

chapters.title: Simon and Cerinthus, False Apostles
chapters.html:
2nd Book of the Covenant 12

The Letter of the Apostles

1The Book of the Covenant that Jesus Christ revealed to His disciples. In it is told how Jesus Christ revealed this book; it is the book of the company of the apostles and of the disciples of Jesus Christ; it is the book meant for all. It was written about Simon and Cerinthus, the false apostles, so that no one may keep company with them, for there is cunning in them, with which they will kill people. We urge you to be firm, not to waver, not to be troubled, and not to turn aside from the word of the Gospel that you have heard. As we heard it, we have written it for the whole world. We have entrusted our sons and our daughters to you in joy, in the name of the Lord, the Father, Master of the world, and in the name of Jesus Christ. May His mercy be great upon you!

Notes

  • The chapter — here the book's second part begins, the apostles' letter to the churches known elsewhere as the Epistle of the Apostles. From here M. R. James's English of the same work is read beside the French; James follows the Coptic where it survives.

  • v1 "The Book of the Covenant" — Guerrier gives the Ethiopic word in parentheses, Kidan, the word that names this book in the canon (see the note on the heading of chapter 1).

  • v1 "As we heard it, we have written it" — the French is broken here (telle que nous… pour le monde entier); James's English has the whole sentence: Like as we heard it, we keep it in remembrance and have written it for the whole world.

  • v1 "with which they will kill people" — so the Ethiopic as Guerrier gives it; James has wherewith they bring men to destruction.

  • Source text — L. Guerrier and S. Grébaut, Le Testament en Galilée de Notre-Seigneur Jésus-Christ, Patrologia Orientalis 9.3 (1913), public domain; read beside M. R. James, The Apocryphal New Testament (1924), public domain. English translation by this project.

speech.text: 2nd Book of the Covenant 12
The Letter of the Apostles

The Book of the Covenant that Jesus Christ revealed to His disciples. In it is told how Jesus Christ revealed this book; it is the book of the company of the apostles and of the disciples of Jesus Christ; it is the book meant for all. It was written about Simon and Cerinthus, the false apostles, so that no one may keep company with them, for there is cunning in them, with which they will kill people. We urge you to be firm, not to waver, not to be troubled, and not to turn aside from the word of the Gospel that you have heard. As we heard it, we have written it for the whole world. We have entrusted our sons and our daughters to you in joy, in the name of the Lord, the Father, Master of the world, and in the name of Jesus Christ. May His mercy be great upon you!

chapters.title: The Apostles' Witness
chapters.html:
2nd Book of the Covenant 13

1We, John and Thomas and Peter and Andrew and James and Philip and Bartholomew and Matthew and Nathanael and Judas the Zealot and Cephas, have written to the churches of the East and the West, of the North and the South, proclaiming and setting out to you what concerns our Lord Jesus Christ. We write what we have heard. We touched Him after He had risen from the dead, and we have written how He revealed to us things great, wonderful and true.

Notes

  • v1 "We write what we have heard. We touched Him" — so the Ethiopic as Guerrier gives it. James's English has according as we have seen and heard and touched him, the words of John's letter: what we have heard, what we have seen with our eyes, what we looked upon and our hands touched (1 John 1:1). The list of eleven names Peter and Cephas as two men.

  • Source text — L. Guerrier and S. Grébaut, Le Testament en Galilée de Notre-Seigneur Jésus-Christ, Patrologia Orientalis 9.3 (1913), public domain; read beside M. R. James, The Apocryphal New Testament (1924), public domain. English translation by this project.
